questions.question: What does the binomial coefficient $\binom nk$ count?
options: The number of ways to choose $k$ objects from $n$ distinct objects without regard to order
The number of ways to arrange all $n$ objects in a line
The probability that every event in a sample space occurs, irrespective of the particular case.
The number of real solutions to an arbitrary equation
questions.explanation: Choosing a $k$-subset amounts to selecting which $k$ of the $n$ elements to include, with no ordering imposed; the count of such subsets is $\binom{n}{k}$.
questions.source_support: The definition says $\binom nk$ counts ways to choose $k$ objects from $n$ distinct objects without regard to order.
option_explanations: Arranging all $n$ objects in a line is counted by $n!$, not $\binom nk$.
It is a count, not a probability that every event occurs.
It has nothing to do with solutions of an arbitrary equation.
